keyFindings.description: Oh My Pi runs the context handler for every transformContext, not only main-loop turns. runEphemeralTurn (BTW, the stop-time self-check via sideTurn), the handoff prompt and buildLiveProviderContext (Anthropic remote compaction) all go through it. The list is appended after the side prompt, each such request waits up to 800 ms, and the remote-compaction slice (length of convert(prefix) applied to convert(prefix+kept)) moves by one. Verified in /opt/omp/bin/omp: runEphemeralTurn -> convertMessagesToLlm -> transformContext Pb -> emitContext. No test covers these paths.

process.exit(0) at the deadline kills the worker in the middle of Bun.spawnSync. runCommand's group kill and rmSync never run, so a slow `!` token command keeps running (detached group) and its stdout file, which holds the bearer token, stays in tmpdir/envoy-command-*. One is left per SessionStart and SubagentStart.

With a `!` token command that does not finish in the ~0.7 s window, no hook ever completes a read or writes answers.json. Every Claude Code start, resume, compaction and subagent then carries the failure line and never the list. The README's recommended token form is a `!` command.

On a failed read, carry() renders the cache. A cache that holds no item in the window (the usual empty list, or items past 72 h) renders undefined, so a session whose Dispatch now refuses (401/5xx/hang) carries nothing and looks the same as 'nothing'. D5 says that must not happen. The cached header also says 'Dispatch did not answer now' for every failure and drops the reason.

S2 filters message_deliveries on session_id, state and created_at, but message_deliveries_session (0051) indexes session_id only. So every model request reads every delivery the session ever received, and the comment at :36-41 (and in 0130) says the opposite. Add a (session_id, created_at) index as 0130 does, or measure it and correct the comments.
The two-copy guard finds only a list that was appended. With an empty list, copy B makes a second HTTP read after A's read settled, so the request can wait up to 2 x 800 ms, past the 1 s bound.
The memory cache, answers.json and the in-flight join are keyed by session only, not by Dispatch URL. If the session's Dispatch changes, a list read from Dispatch A is shown when Dispatch B fails.

Still describes the old reply routing and the old suppressed_authors rule ('on a reply only the thread's root author'). The new route of a reply to the document's credited sessions and comment_create.go's new rule are missing.

Says a GIN index would end HOT updates. The outbox's recordBatch update already sets published_at and next_attempt_at, which events_unpublished and events_unpublished_ready use, so those updates are not HOT now. The same claim is in cmd/dispatch/README.md:876.

Cleanup: the feature's read model (relation precedence, dispatch:// and href shapes) is in the infrastructure package store, which now imports contracts and model, and it adds a fifth copy of the Queryer interface. Move it to its own package, as asks, events and refs are.
Cleanup: loadThreadDocument copies loadRootCommentAuthor's recursive query, and the reply branch runs both on the same id. Use one loadThreadRoot that returns the author and the document.

Cleanup: writeCacheFile copies dispatch-session-state's writeAtomically because of an import cycle, and the copies already differ. Both hosts also repeat the sessionDirectory try/catch. Move the state-dir helpers to a leaf module.

Cleanup: sessionAnswersText repeats replyAddress's session resolution. Other duplicates: the owner rendering at session-answers.ts:83 repeats openAskOwner (dispatch-execute.ts:2169), and the message helpers in dispatch-first.ts are now shared.
Cleanup after cutover: no production caller now passes getComments' artifact parameter. Also, hooks-timeout.test.ts:9 names ANSWERS_SETTLED_BY_MS, which does not exist.
